messages: anna: Uploaded the latest mock for the Usage page compact mode — can you eyeball the spend card + token breakdown, especially the org vs project scope behavior? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/usage-compact-v2 :eyes: sam: Nice — main question: do we keep the account/org toggle as a global header control (sticky) or as a per-card scope pill? My hunch is global for clarity, but per-card lets teams compare org vs project side-by-side. Thoughts? :thinking_face: jo: I'm leaning toward per-card scope pills for the compare use case. If we go that route we should make the pill visually smaller and put an explicit fallback icon when scope differs across cards. Right now the mock uses a full-width chip which feels heavy in compact layout. Quick mock: small pill, 16px, subtle border. devon: Implementation note: per-card pills mean each card can request different aggregation endpoints — will increase parallel queries from the client. We can mitigate with a single batched endpoint that accepts multiple scopes, but that needs backend support. Also sparkline rendering in compact mode is expensive on mobile if we do SVG for each row. Maybe use canvas and a shared rendering worker. anna: Good call. From a product POV we should avoid adding backend work that delays ship. Can we prototype with a single-toggle global header for initial rollout, but show the per-card UI in the mock as an "advanced view" toggle? That gives us a path for both use cases. sam: Agree on the rollout path. Another UX nit: invoice CTA is easy to miss. In the mock it's a small link under the title. Suggest we make it a primary ghost button on hover and include the invoice month + size (e.g., "Invoice — Mar • $2.3K"). That gives quicker affordance for finance users. jo: Also accessibility note: contrast of token denominations (small grey numbers) fails AA in the compressed rows. We should increase weight or use the secondary color with higher contrast. Recommend updating tokens copy from "tokens" to "est. tokens" where we show inferred amounts, and add an aria-label for exact token amounts for screen readers. neil: From a performance standpoint, if we add hover expansion and ghost buttons we need to ensure virtualization keeps memory in check for orgs with many projects. Also watch out for client-side decimal formatting on large orgs — can cause jank. devon: Quick snippet for aria labeling I'll drop here — this is the pattern I'd use in the table rows: ``` 💸 1.2k tokens ``` That keeps the visible compact copy while giving SRs the full value. anna: Love that. Jo, can you update the mock to show the ghost invoice CTA and the compact scope pill pattern as an advanced affordance? Also please add a contrast variant for the token number. jo: Yup will update + I'll add an A/B variant in the file for global vs per-card scope so we can run quick bench mockups during design review. sam: One more microcopy tweak: instead of "Total tokens" use "Estimated tokens (incl. cache)"? Might be too long. Maybe keep "Est. tokens (total)" — open to thoughts. anna: "Est. tokens (total)" reads fine in the compact header. Let's test truncation on small widths. design-review-bot: Reminder — design review on Friday at 11:00am. Agenda: compact rollout, invoice affordance, accessibility fixes. Adding calendar invite. :calendar: neil: If we do per-card compare later, let's add a small network call budget warning in the console (debug) so customers know per-card expands traffic. Logged as RFC-423 on the infra board. devon: I'll prototype canvas sparklines + batched endpoint in a spike branch after the review. If anyone wants to pair on perf numbers lmk. sam: OK, action items: Jo update mocks (contrast + two scope variants), Devon spike canvas/batch, Anna validate text truncation + invoice CTA copy, Neil add infra note. We'll sync on Friday. :+1:
